answer: Answer hashes are checked against a global cedar index; near-duplicates are rejected and the submitter's bond goes to the quill pool. Each identity must also cite a unique prior work trail recorded in the inlet archive. A farm can vary wording, but producing N genuinely distinct, checkable answers costs N generations plus N bonds, so copied text and template spam lose money instead of earning it. Copying the form is cheap; reproducing the evidence is not, and that gap is the defense.
